Kuvitus: lentokoneen istuimen tarjottime: Illustration: on the tray table of an aeroplane seat there is a swollen, tight bag of crisps and a mug of water. Through the window clouds can be seen far below.
Mikromalli Boylen laista, kaaviokuva. Va: Micro model of Boyle's law, schematic picture. On the left, a cylinder contains eight gas particles in volume V at pressure p. On the right, the same eight particles have been squeezed by pressing the piston to half the volume, V/2, at the same temperature. The velocity arrows are equally long, but there are twice as many hit marks on the piston and the bottom, so the pressure is 2p. The heights of the gas spaces are in the ratio 2 : 1.
Kaksi kuvaajaa samoista mittauksista, mi: Two graphs of the same measurements, to scale, when pV = 2000 kPa·ml. Above, pressure as a function of volume is a falling curve; the measurement points V = 10, 15, 20, 30 and 40 ml are on the curve. Below, pressure as a function of the reciprocal of the volume, 1/V, is a straight line through the origin whose slope is pV.
Kuvaajat mittakaavassa, kun T on 0–400 K: Graphs to scale when T is 0–400 K. Above, the volume of a gas at constant pressure, below, the pressure of a gas at constant volume, as a function of the temperature in kelvins. The measurement points between 253 and 373 K are on a straight line. The extension of the line, drawn dashed, passes through the origin: the volume or the pressure would be zero at absolute zero, 0 K, that is, −273 °C.
Kaksi tilanmuutosta, kaaviokuva. Vasemma: Two changes of state, schematic picture. On the left, an isobaric change: the piston of the cylinder is loaded by an object of constant weight, so when the gas warms from temperature T₁ to temperature T₂, the piston rises and the volume increases from V₁ to V₂; the velocity arrows of the particles are longer. On the right, an isochoric change: the volume V of a rigid, closed container stays the same, and when the gas warms, the needle of the pressure gauge turns to the greater pressure p₂.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: ilman paine p til: Graph to scale: air pressure p as a function of volume V at constant temperature, five measurement points without a drawn curve. The points are (10 ml; 200 kPa), (15 ml; 133 kPa), (20 ml; 100 kPa), (30 ml; 67 kPa) and (40 ml; 50 kPa). The grid spacing is 5 ml and 25 kPa.
